newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy recovers remains of two drowned Albanians.
newsitem.headline: Italy recovers remains of two drowned Albanians.

text.p: Marine researchers recovered the remains of two Albanians from the depths of the Adriatic Sea on Tuesday more than six weeks after their boat sank in a collision with an Italian navy vessel.

Deputy prosecutor Leonardo de Castris, who is investigating the March 28 disaster, said the decomposed corpse of a woman and a skeleton had been brought some to the surface from a depth of some 800 metres (2,500 feet) by a remote-controlled submarine.
The device was operated from a marine research vessel, The Performer, which Italian authorities have commissioned to probe the wreck of the Albanian boat.
Albanian authorities say at least 83 Albanians drowned when the boat, which had set out for Italy from the southern port of Vlore packed with refugees, was in collision with the corvette Sibilla.
The incident took place during patrolling of the Adriatic by the Italian navy to try to stem a flood of thousands of Albanians who had headed for Italy to escape unrest sweeping their country.
De Castris said the body of the woman had been recovered after cameras on the submarine device showed an arm poking from one of the sunken wreck's portholes.

The skeleton was found near the vessel. Both sets of remains, the first found since the sinking, were being taken to the southeast Italian port of Brindisi and De Castris said more bodies were inside the wreck.

"You can see something but it is still not possible to establish the number of bodies. What is sure is that we are not dealing with the 'piles of corpses' I have read about in some newspapers," De Castris told reporters in Brindisi.

Italian rescue ships picked up 34 survivors and four dead on the night of the sinking, which raised tensions with Albania ahead of the dispatch of an Italian-led security force now deployed in the impoverished Balkan country.
Italy has rejected accounts of some survivors that the Sibilla rammed the refugee boat, which Rome says was badly overcrowded and ran into the path of the corvette as it tried to dodge past it.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has promised that every effort will be made to recover all the dead from the bottom of the sea.
